title: ZPC compliance: benchmarks, ignore rules and security policies

benchmark-types.statement: The Supported Benchmarks page says ZPC supports benchmarks such as Cybersecurity Benchmarks, Laws and Regulations, and Industry benchmarks.

quotes: ZPC supports many compliance benchmarks such as Cybersecurity Benchmarks, Laws and Regulations, and Industry benchmarks.

cis-foundations-versions.statement: The supported-benchmarks tables list these Center for Internet Security foundations benchmark versions: AWS v1.5.0 and v2.0.0; Microsoft Azure v1.4.0, v1.5.0 and v2.0.0; Google Cloud Platform v1.3.0 and v2.0.0; OCI v1.2.0.

quotes: Center for Internet Security AWS Foundations Benchmark v1.5.0
Center for Internet Security AWS Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0
Center for Internet Security Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v1.4.0
Center for Internet Security Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v1.5.0
Center for Internet Security Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0
Center for Internet Security Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark v1.3.0
Center for Internet Security Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark v2.0.0
Center for Internet Security OCI Foundations Benchmark v1.2.0

k8s-benchmark-versions.statement: The supported-benchmarks table for Kubernetes lists Center for Internet Security Kubernetes Benchmark v1.6.1 and v1.7.1 and the Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Benchmark v1.4.0.

quotes: Center for Internet Security Kubernetes Benchmark v1.6.1
Center for Internet Security Kubernetes Benchmark v1.7.1
Center for Internet Security Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Benchmark v1.4.0

best-practices-benchmark.statement: ZPC compiles the policies from all benchmarks into a Zscaler Best Practices benchmark for gauging compliance across all available benchmarks.

quotes: ZPC also compiles the policies offered in all the benchmarks and offers a Zscaler Best Practices benchmark for you to gauge your compliance across all available benchmarks.

benchmark-table-fields.statement: Each benchmark in the compliance benchmark table shows its type (predefined or custom), policy count, compliance score percentage, and a State toggle that enables or disables the benchmark.

quotes: Type: View whether the benchmark is predefined or custom.
Policy Count: View the policy count in the benchmark.
Compliance Score: View the compliance score percentage of your cloud deployment for the benchmark.
State: Use the toggle bar to enable or disable the benchmark.

ignore-rule-fields.statement: Each compliance ignore rule shows a Rule Scope listing the security policies, cloud accounts, tags, assets and regions it applies to, and an End Date on which the rule is going to be disabled.

quotes: Rule Scope: The list of security policies, cloud accounts, tags, assets, and regions on which the rule is applied.
End Date: The date the compliance ignore rule is going to be disabled.

custom-benchmark-creation.statement: The Creating a New Benchmark page says a custom benchmark is built from 300+ security policies, can be filtered by business units, clouds and accounts, and needs categories added in the Selected Policies pane before policies can be moved from the Available Policies pane.

quotes: You can choose from 300+ security policies and add to your custom benchmarks
Business units are logical groups of multiple cloud accounts.
Business Units: Select one or multiple business units.
Clouds: Select one or multiple cloud service providers.
Accounts: Select one or multiple cloud accounts.
In the Selected Policies pane, you need to add categories before moving security policies from the Available Policies pane:

policy-status-values.statement: On the benchmark details page a policy status is Passed, Failed, No Resources, Manual, Disabled or Ignored; a security policy passes only when all assets pass.

quotes: A security policy passes only when all assets pass.
No Resources: The security policy cannot be evaluated by ZPC as it does not have necessary resources.
Manual: The security policy requires you to manually offer information for ZPC to evaluate it.
Disabled: The security policy is disabled and is not being evaluated by ZPC.
Ignored: The security policy is ignored and not being evaluated by ZPC.
Passed: The security policy has passed for all relevant assets.
Failed: The security policy has failed for all relevant assets.

policy-severity-static.statement: The benchmark details page describes policy severity as a static value of Critical, High, Medium or Low signaling the severity of policy failure.

quotes: Severity: Static value signaling the severity of policy failure. The value can be Critical, High, Medium, or Low.

benchmark-details-trend-export.statement: The benchmark details page shows a passed and failed policy trend over the last 30 days and exports the details as a PDF file; for a newly enabled benchmark the trend appears only after 24 hours.

quotes: View Policy Compliance Trend: View the passed and failed policy trend over the last 30 days.
Export the benchmark details as a PDF file.
If you have just enabled a benchmark, ZPC shows the Policy Compliance Trend only after 24 hours.

disabled-benchmark-date.statement: For a disabled compliance benchmark, ZPC lets you view the last date the compliance information was generated.

quotes: If you disabled a compliance benchmark, you can view the last date when the compliance information was generated.

compliance-policy-allow-skip.statement: Allow Skip on a compliance security policy is enabled by default and lets developers skip the policy in their code repository or CI/CD tool by adding skip comments; if disabled, skip comments have no effect.

quotes: Allow Skip is enabled by default and lets developers skip the policy in their code repository or CI/CD tool by adding skip comments.
If it's disabled, the policy cannot be skipped even if the developers add skip comments.

compliance-policy-tabs.statement: The Compliance tab of the compliance security policy details page shows the benchmark name, domain and control section.

quotes: On the Compliance tab, you can view the following compliance details:
Compliance: The compliance benchmark name.
Domain: The compliance benchmark domain.
Control Section: The control section of the compliance benchmark.

ignore-policy-effect.statement: Ignoring a compliance security policy also ignores all its relevant assets and sets the policy status to Ignored; ZPC counts ignored policies as passed in the compliance score.

quotes: When a compliance security policy is ignored, all relevant assets for that policy are also ignored by ZPC.
When you ignore a policy, its status changes to "Ignored". ZPC categorizes ignored policies as passed for its compliance score evaluation.

ignore-asset-effect.statement: Ignoring an asset sets its status to Ignored, and ZPC counts ignored assets as passed in the compliance score; ignoring an asset for one policy does not stop ZPC evaluating other compliance policies against it.

quotes: When you ignore an asset, its status changes to "Ignored". ZPC categorizes ignored assets as passed for its compliance score evaluation.
When you ignore an asset for a particular policy, ZPC continues to evaluate other compliance policy against the asset.

include-assets-after-policy-ignore.statement: If a compliance security policy is ignored, assets can be manually included for evaluation against that policy, and including a policy also includes all its relevant assets.

quotes: When a compliance security policy is ignored, all relevant assets for that policy are also ignored by ZPC.
If you need some assets to be evaluated by ZPC for the same security policy, you can manually include those assets for ZPC evaluation.
When you include a compliance security policy, all relevant assets are also included.

auto-ignore-scope-defaults.statement: An automatic compliance ignore rule has Policies, Cloud Accounts, Tags, Assets and Regions scope filters, each defaulting to its All option (All Policies, All Accounts, All Tags, All Assets, All Regions).

quotes: By default, the All Policies filter is selected.
By default, the All Accounts filter is selected.
By default, the All Tags filter is selected.
By default, the All Assets filter is selected.
By default, the All Regions filter is selected.

auto-ignore-scope-options.statement: In an automatic ignore rule, policies can be scoped by severity or selection, cloud accounts by provider (AWS, Azure, GCP or Kubernetes), tags by native cloud service provider tags, and assets by asset type or asset category.

quotes: Severity: Select the required Policy Severity from the drop-down menu.
Select Policies: Select to view the Select Existing Policies page, and select the required policies from the table.
Cloud Provider: Select the cloud provider (AWS, Azure, GCP, or Kubernetes).
You can select resources to ignore based on native cloud service provider tags.
Asset Type: Select the required Asset Type from the drop-down menu. For example, S3 buckets or EC2 instances.
Asset Category: Select the required Asset Category from the drop-down menu. For example, Analytics or Compute.

auto-ignore-end-date-effect.statement: The Ignore Rule End Date is optional and sets when the rule should no longer be applied; ZPC ignores all assets and policies matching the filter for the compliance score evaluation.

quotes: Ignore Rule End Date (Optional): Use the drop-down menu to select when the ignore rule should no longer be applied.
ZPC ignores all assets and policies matching the compliance ignore filter for the compliance score evaluation.

policy-catalog.statement: The About Security Policies page says ZPC offers over 400 security policies across multiple cloud service providers, covering both runtime and buildtime environments, and that the security policies cannot be modified but custom security policies can be created.

quotes: ZPC offers over 400 security policies across multiple cloud service providers (CSPs), including Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform.
ZPC has created security policies to protect both your runtime and buildtime environments.
The security policies cannot be modified, but you can create new custom security policies tailored for your cloud deployment.

policy-attributes.statement: The About Security Policies page lists a theme attribute (Compliance, Security Exposure, Security Events or Blank) and a threat category attribute (Ransomware, Misconfiguration or Account Takeover) for security policies.

quotes: Theme: The security policy theme (Compliance, Security Exposure, Security Events, or Blank).
Threat Category: The security policy threat category (Ransomware, Misconfiguration, or Account Takeover).

policy-focus.statement: Policy Focus indicates whether a policy focuses on an asset or identity misconfiguration.

quotes: Policy Focus: Whether the policy focuses on an asset or identity misconfiguration.

cloud-policy-state-disabled.statement: On the Cloud Policies tab, a disabled policy is not run against the collected configuration metadata.

quotes: On the Cloud Policies tab, you can do the following:
When disabled, the policy is not run against the collected configuration metadata.
evidence.after: Remediation Enabled: Whether remediation is enabled for the alerts generated by the policy.

iac-allow-skip.statement: On the IaC Policies tab, the Allow Skip toggle is enabled by default and lets developers skip the policy by adding skip comments in their code repository or CI/CD tool; if disabled, skip comments have no effect.

quotes: To view the IaC Policies tab, go to Policies > IaC Policies.

The Allow Skip toggle is enabled by default and lets developers skip the policy in their code repository or CI/CD tool by adding skip comments. If it's disabled, the policy cannot be skipped even if the developers add skip comments.

policy-details-alerts-tab.statement: The security policy details Alerts tab shows alert status as Open, Closed or Resolved and the resource name (Identity Name or Asset Name).

quotes: On the Alerts tab, you can do the following:
Resource Name: The resource name (Identity Name or Asset Name).
Status: The status (Open, Closed, or Resolved) of the alert.

delete-custom-closes-alerts.statement: Deleting a custom security policy closes all alerts previously generated by it.

quotes: When you delete a custom policy, all alerts previously generated by the policy are closed.

edit-custom-effects.statement: Editing custom-policy information such as title or remediation procedure is reflected in the Alerts page and Cloud Threats dashboard, while editing the query logic closes all existing alerts and generates new ones from the new logic.

quotes: If you edit the custom policy information, such as policy title or remediation procedure, the new information reflects in the Alerts page and the Cloud Threats dashboard.
If you edit the custom policy query logic, ZPC determines that the custom policy has changed and closes all existing alerts. It generates new alerts based on the new custom policy query logic.

remediation-prereq.statement: Remediation of alerts from a policy can be allowed when Support Remediation is enabled for the policy, and bulk changes need policies whose Supports Remediation column is Yes.

quotes: You can allow remediation of alerts generated by a specific policy when Support Remediation is enabled for the policy.
Select the checkboxes for the security policies you want to allow or disallow remediation and the Supports Remediation column is set to Yes.

custom-policy-compliance-prereq.statement: Compliance details can be entered on a custom policy only when its query logic is focused on assets and the asset type predicate is defined.

quotes: To enter compliance details, the query logic must be focused on assets and the asset type predicate has to be defined.

custom-policy-scope.statement: The Creating Custom Security Policies page says custom security policies extend coverage beyond the 300+ predefined policies, including to asset types without predefined policies; a policy focuses on Assets or Identities.

quotes: ZPC supports creating custom security policies to expand security coverage to your cloud infrastructure beyond the 300+ predefined security policies.
Add a new custom security policy to asset types that currently do not have predefined security policies.
Under Focus on, select either Assets or Identities.

policy-state-severity-change.statement: The Managing Security Policies page says ZPC offers enabling or disabling a policy and setting policy severity for individual and bulk security policies, and the steps for each start from the Cloud Policies or IaC Policies tab.

quotes: ZPC offers actions such as enabling or disabling a policy, allowing or disallowing remediation on a policy, or setting policy severity for individual and bulk security policies.
On the Policies page, click the Cloud Policies or IaC Policies tab.

quotes: On the Policies page, click the Cloud Policies or IaC Policies tab.
On the Policies page, click the Cloud Policies or IaC Policies tab.

quotes: On the Policies page, click the Cloud Policies or IaC Policies tab.

service-status.title: Whether the ZPC features these pages describe are still available
service-status.detail: portfolio.cloud-protection records ZPC end of life as planned for March 15, 2026. None of the captured posture pages says whether it describes a service still available or carries a product-version statement, so none of the compliance or policy facts here is claimed as current.

score-formula.title: How the compliance score is calculated, and whether partial failures show Failed
score-formula.detail: The pages say ignored policies and assets count as passed, and that a policy passes only when all assets pass, but give no score formula. The benchmark details page does not say whether a policy that fails for only some assets shows Failed (its Failed status reads "failed for all relevant assets").

shared-benchmark-rows.title: Which benchmarks the Kubernetes and OCI tables list beyond the Center for Internet Security versions
shared-benchmark-rows.detail: The AWS, Azure and GCP table rows are claimed in cloud-tables-shared-benchmarks. The EKS, AKS and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 rows of the Kubernetes table and the NIST row of the OCI table repeat rows quoted elsewhere and are not claimed; the GCP table names its Kubernetes benchmark "GKE - Kubernetes Benchmark v1.4.0" where the Kubernetes table says "Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Benchmark v1.4.0".

admin-permissions-limits.title: Which admin roles and limits apply to policies, benchmarks and ignore rules
admin-permissions-limits.detail: zpc.roles records the predefined roles matrix (zpc.roles:matrix-admin-viewonly-secops, zpc.roles:matrix-compliance-iac) and the global modules list (zpc.roles:global-modules-list), which includes Policies, IaC Policies and Ignore Rules. No captured page maps those roles to the actions of ignoring policies, creating policies or benchmarks or changing severity, or states limits on custom benchmarks or ignore rules.
